{"id":"mimid-1wgh.46.20.1.1","title":"[telemetry] exports metrics and logs but no spans, while reporting traces=true","description":"Found 2026-11-22 while turning on OpenTelemetry for the interop host.
mimid starts, logs "OpenTelemetry export configured ... traces=true",
and exports metrics and logs but NOT ONE span.

MEASURED, with a collector on loopback writing every signal to a file:

  batches:     {'resourceMetrics': 10, 'resourceLogs': 7, 'resourceSpans': 1}
  log records: 44
  spans:       [('handmade', 1)]

'handmade' is a span I POSTed to the collector by hand as a control, so
the only span in the file is the one mimid did not send. Metrics and
logs arrive continuously; spans never do.

RULED OUT, in this order:
- The collector. A hand-made POST to http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces
  returns 200 and lands in the file, so the receiver, the traces
  pipeline and the file exporter all work.
- The endpoint and transport. telemetry.rs builds all three exporters
  with .with_http() and the standard paths (/v1/traces, /v1/logs,
  /v1/metrics) against the same base URL. Metrics and logs on that base
  URL work, so the base URL and HTTP transport are right.
- The log filter level. Spans are at default INFO
  (#[tracing::instrument(name = "protocol_request", ...)] in http.rs with
  no `level =` anywhere in the file), and RUST_LOG is unset so the
  filter is "info". Setting RUST_LOG=info,mimid_server=trace changed
  nothing: still no spans.
- A missing flush. Restarting mimid runs Telemetry::shutdown, which
  calls tracer.shutdown(), and no spans appeared across several
  restarts.

WHERE THAT POINTS. Metrics go through a separate path (the global meter
and the Metrics struct), while traces and logs BOTH come from
Telemetry::layers() into the tracing subscriber. Logs work, so the layer
stack is installed and reaching the subscriber. So the fault is specific
to the traces half: tracing_opentelemetry::layer().with_tracer(
provider.tracer("mimid")), composed by Layer::and_then(traces, logs) in
telemetry.rs layers().

Not chased further here, because logs plus metrics already give the
interop day what it needs and this is a code investigation rather than a
deployment step. Worth looking at whether the Option<OpenTelemetryLayer>
in that and_then is being applied, and whether the SdkTracerProvider
needs to be installed globally for the layer's tracer to record.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: spans are the signal that makes a failed
interop exchange legible -- which endpoint, which peer, how long, and
the `peer` field each protocol_request span records. Logs give the
events but not the correlation. Also, the startup line says traces=true
when nothing is exported, so an operator has no way to notice.

LIVE STATE, and it is useful as it stands: a collector runs on dokr
(docker container otelcol-mimid, OTLP on 127.0.0.1:4318 only, no UI, no
outbound network) writing every signal to
/var/log/otelcol-mimid/mimid-telemetry.jsonl, rotating at 64 MB with 5
backups. mimid's [telemetry] points at it. So the interop day will leave
a greppable record of metrics and log events; only spans are missing.

Two deployment notes for anyone redoing this:
- The collector image runs as uid 10001. The output directory must be
  owned by it; root-owned 755 fails with "can't open new logfile ...
  permission denied" and the collector drops every batch while looking
  healthy.
- Those errors appear only in `docker logs otelcol-mimid`, not in
  mimid's journal, because mimid's exporter considers a buffered send
  successful.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-23T05:17:59.60136893Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-23T05:17:59.60136893Z","labels":["interop"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-1wgh.46.20.1.1","depends_on_id":"mimid-1wgh.46.20.1","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-23T05:17:59.636235877Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"notes":"CORRECTED 2026-11-22: THERE IS NO EXPORT BUG. The description above is
wrong and this bead should not have been filed as a defect. My test
traffic produced no spans to export.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS, verified:

  RUST_LOG=debug, 4 directory fetches  -> 4 http_request spans exported
  RUST_LOG=debug, 3 refused requests   -> 0 additional spans

So the export path works end to end. Two separate things hid every span,
and both are ordinary behaviour:

1. THE HTTP SPAN IS AT DEBUG. http.rs:144 creates it with
   tracing::debug_span!("http_request", ...). RUST_LOG is unset on the
   host, so the filter is "info" and the span is never created. Metrics
   and log records are unaffected, which is exactly the pattern I
   misread as "traces are broken".

2. A REFUSED REQUEST NEVER REACHES A SPAN. provider_auth::check is
   layered OUTSIDE the router in main.rs:390, so for an unsigned request
   it returns refuse() before tower-http's TraceLayer runs and before any
   handler's INFO protocol_request span is entered. Almost all my test
   traffic was unsigned identifierQuery, i.e. the one shape that produces
   nothing.

That also explains why my earlier attempt with
RUST_LOG=info,mimid_server=trace showed nothing: the level was right by
then, but the traffic was still refused requests.

MY ERROR, and it is the fifth of this session: I filed a defect against
mimid for the output of my own test setup. Bead mimid-7yn7.9 exists for
exactly this and its rule -- rule out our own bug first -- is what caught
it, but only after the bead was already written. The rule needs applying
before filing, not after.

WHAT IS GENUINELY WORTH FIXING, and it is point 2, reframed:

A provider-authentication refusal produces NO SPAN AT ALL. On an interop
day the refusals are the interesting events: a peer whose signature or
certificate we rejected is precisely what someone needs to see. Today
that event exists only as a DEBUG log line, with no span, no latency, no
trace id to correlate with the peer's own view.

Two ways to close it, both small:
- Move the provider_auth::check layer INSIDE the trace layer, so a
  refused request is still wrapped in http_request. Check what that does
  to the certificate layer's ordering, since forwarded_certificate must
  still run before check reads the certificate.
- Or give check its own span rather than only tracing::debug! events.
  That keeps the layer order untouched and is probably the smaller
  change.

Also worth deciding separately: whether http_request should be an INFO
span rather than DEBUG. Making it INFO would mean telemetry yields
traces at the default level, which is what an operator who configures
[telemetry] plainly expects; it was presumably DEBUG to keep the text
log quiet, and now that the span can go to a collector instead those two
goals have come apart.

LIVE STATE: /etc/systemd/system/mimid.service.d/99-spandiag.conf sets
RUST_LOG=debug on the host with a comment saying why, since otherwise
the collector that was just deployed records no traces at all. Verified:
spans now export."}

wrong and this bead should not have been filed as a defect. My test
traffic produced no spans to export.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS, verified:

  RUST_LOG=debug, 4 directory fetches  -> 4 http_request spans exported
  RUST_LOG=debug, 3 refused requests   -> 0 additional spans

So the export path works end to end. Two separate things hid every span,
and both are ordinary behaviour:

1. THE HTTP SPAN IS AT DEBUG. http.rs:144 creates it with
   tracing::debug_span!("http_request", ...). RUST_LOG is unset on the
   host, so the filter is "info" and the span is never created. Metrics
   and log records are unaffected, which is exactly the pattern I
   misread as "traces are broken".

2. A REFUSED REQUEST NEVER REACHES A SPAN. provider_auth::check is
   layered OUTSIDE the router in main.rs:390, so for an unsigned request
   it returns refuse() before tower-http's TraceLayer runs and before any
   handler's INFO protocol_request span is entered. Almost all my test
   traffic was unsigned identifierQuery, i.e. the one shape that produces
   nothing.

That also explains why my earlier attempt with
RUST_LOG=info,mimid_server=trace showed nothing: the level was right by
then, but the traffic was still refused requests.

mimid for the output of my own test setup. Bead mimid-7yn7.9 exists for
exactly this and its rule -- rule out our own bug first -- is what caught
it, but only after the bead was already written. The rule needs applying
before filing, not after.

WHAT IS GENUINELY WORTH FIXING, and it is point 2, reframed:

A provider-authentication refusal produces NO SPAN AT ALL. On an interop
day the refusals are the interesting events: a peer whose signature or
certificate we rejected is precisely what someone needs to see. Today
that event exists only as a DEBUG log line, with no span, no latency, no
trace id to correlate with the peer's own view.

Two ways to close it, both small:
- Move the provider_auth::check layer INSIDE the trace layer, so a
  refused request is still wrapped in http_request. Check what that does
  to the certificate layer's ordering, since forwarded_certificate must
  still run before check reads the certificate.
- Or give check its own span rather than only tracing::debug! events.
  That keeps the layer order untouched and is probably the smaller
  change.

Also worth deciding separately: whether http_request should be an INFO
span rather than DEBUG. Making it INFO would mean telemetry yields
traces at the default level, which is what an operator who configures
[telemetry] plainly expects; it was presumably DEBUG to keep the text
log quiet, and now that the span can go to a collector instead those two
goals have come apart.

WHAT SHIPPED.

provider_auth::check opens `provider_auth` at INFO over the whole layer,
with peer, endpoint, outcome (authenticated | refused | observed) and then
mechanism or reason. It is opened before the body is read, not just around
the mechanisms, so that EVERY return from this layer is inside it: an
oversized body (413) and an unparseable target (400) are `refused` with
their reason too, not only an authentication failure. The cost of that
choice is that the span's duration includes reading the body, so it is the
layer's cost and not the mechanisms' alone; said so in the module doc. It is entered for the DEBUG events that follow, so each
of those carries the span and an exported log record carries its trace id --
which is the correlation the bead said was missing. It is dropped before the
handler runs, because a span guard must not be held across an await and the
handler has protocol_request of its own.

trace layer, or giving check its own span. Took the second, as the bead
guessed was smaller. Moving the layer would mean router() in http.rs taking
the check middleware as a parameter, since it applies the trace layer
itself, and every test that calls router() would change. The cost of not
moving it: a refused request still has no `http_request`, so its trace has
no route or status. Recorded on the new bead below.
